title: Cybersecurity Engineering
description: Networking and operating-system foundations, offensive and defensive practice, application and cloud security, and the incident response skills that turn knowledge into a job.

steps.title: How networks actually work
steps.description: The OSI and TCP/IP models, packets, routing, NAT and the full path a request takes. Almost every attack and defence is easier to reason about once this is solid.

steps.title: Core protocols
steps.description: TCP, UDP, DNS, HTTP, TLS and DHCP in detail, including handshakes and failure modes. Read real traffic rather than only diagrams.

steps.title: Packet analysis
steps.description: Capture and read traffic in Wireshark: follow a stream, spot a scan, and recognise plaintext credentials. Seeing bytes on the wire makes theory concrete.

steps.title: Linux fundamentals
steps.description: Filesystem layout, users and groups, permissions, processes, systemd and logs. Most servers you defend or attack run Linux.

steps.title: Windows and Active Directory
steps.description: Windows internals, the registry, event logs, Kerberos and AD structure. Enterprise compromise is usually an Active Directory story.

steps.title: Scripting for security
steps.description: Python for automation and tooling, plus enough Bash and PowerShell to move around a host. Repetitive analysis should always become a script.

steps.title: Cryptography foundations
steps.description: Symmetric and asymmetric encryption, hashing, digital signatures, certificates and PKI. Learn why rolling your own is always the wrong answer.

steps.title: Build a home lab
steps.description: Set up isolated VMs with a vulnerable target, an attacker box and a monitoring host. Never practise on systems you do not own or have written permission to test.

steps.title: Reconnaissance
steps.description: Passive OSINT and active scanning with Nmap: host discovery, service and version detection, and reading results without triggering every alarm.

steps.title: Vulnerability assessment
steps.description: Enumerate services, map findings to CVEs, and score severity with CVSS. Learn to separate a real risk from a scanner's noise.

steps.title: Web application security: the OWASP Top 10
steps.description: Broken access control, injection, cryptographic failures, SSRF and the rest — what each looks like in code and how each is fixed.

steps.title: Hands-on web exploitation
steps.description: Work through deliberately vulnerable labs covering SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, IDOR and authentication flaws, in a lab you control.

steps.title: Intercepting proxies
steps.description: Use Burp Suite to intercept, modify and replay requests, and to fuzz parameters methodically rather than by guesswork.

steps.title: Authentication and session security
steps.description: Password storage, MFA, OAuth 2.0, OIDC, JWT pitfalls and session fixation. Auth bugs are consistently the highest-impact findings.

steps.title: Secure coding practices
steps.description: Input validation, parameterised queries, output encoding, safe deserialisation and dependency management. Prevention beats detection.

steps.title: Threat modelling
steps.description: Apply STRIDE to a design, enumerate trust boundaries and rank mitigations. Cheapest security work you will ever do, done before code exists.

steps.title: Privilege escalation
steps.description: Local escalation paths on Linux and Windows: misconfigured permissions, SUID binaries, scheduled tasks and credential reuse.

steps.title: Post-exploitation and lateral movement
steps.description: Persistence, credential dumping and pivoting through a network — understood primarily so you can detect and block it.

steps.title: Malware analysis basics
steps.description: Static and dynamic analysis in a sandbox, strings and hashes, and recognising packing and obfuscation. Detonate only in isolation.

steps.title: Logging and SIEM
steps.description: Centralise logs, write detection rules and cut alert noise. Detection engineering is where most defensive jobs actually sit.

steps.title: Threat detection and hunting
steps.description: Map detections to MITRE ATT&CK techniques and hunt proactively on a hypothesis rather than waiting for an alert.

steps.title: Incident response
steps.description: The preparation, identification, containment, eradication, recovery and lessons-learned cycle, plus evidence handling and chain of custody.

steps.title: Digital forensics
steps.description: Disk and memory imaging, timeline analysis and artefact recovery, with enough rigour that findings would survive scrutiny.

steps.title: Network defence architecture
steps.description: Firewalls, IDS and IPS, segmentation, zero trust and defence in depth. Design so that one compromise is not total compromise.

steps.title: Cloud security
steps.description: IAM policies, misconfigured storage, security groups, secrets management and the shared responsibility model across AWS, Azure and GCP.

steps.title: Container and Kubernetes security
steps.description: Image scanning, rootless containers, admission control, network policies and RBAC. Container defaults are convenient, not safe.

steps.title: DevSecOps
steps.description: Shift security left with SAST, DAST, dependency and secret scanning wired into CI so problems surface at pull-request time.

steps.title: Governance, risk and compliance
steps.description: ISO 27001, SOC 2, NIST CSF and GDPR — the frameworks that shape what security teams are actually funded to do.

steps.title: Capture the flag practice
steps.description: Compete regularly across web, crypto, forensics and pwn categories. CTFs build the pattern recognition that certifications alone do not.

steps.title: Reporting and communication
steps.description: Write findings with clear impact, reproduction steps and remediation advice for both engineers and executives. An unread report fixes nothing.

steps.title: Capstone: secure and attack your own stack
steps.description: Deploy a realistic application, attack it, document every finding, then fix and re-test it with detections in place. Show the full loop.

title: Mobile Development with React Native
description: Ship cross-platform apps properly — navigation, state, native modules, offline storage, performance profiling, and getting through both app store review processes.

steps.title: JavaScript and modern syntax
steps.description: Closures, promises, async/await, destructuring, modules and array methods. React Native is JavaScript first — gaps here surface as confusing bugs later.

steps.title: TypeScript for React Native
steps.description: Types, interfaces, generics and typing props and navigation params. TypeScript is effectively the default for new React Native projects.

steps.title: React fundamentals
steps.description: Components, props, state, the rendering cycle and reconciliation. React Native is React with different primitives, so learn React properly first.

steps.title: React hooks in depth
steps.description: useState, useEffect, useMemo, useCallback, useRef and custom hooks, plus the dependency-array rules that cause most re-render bugs.

steps.title: React Native core concepts
steps.description: View, Text, Image, ScrollView and the bridge between JavaScript and native. Understand what the framework is actually doing under your components.

steps.title: Choosing Expo or bare workflow
steps.description: Expo's managed workflow versus bare React Native — build tooling, native module access and ejection costs. Choose deliberately at the start.

steps.title: Layout with Flexbox
steps.description: Flex direction, justify, align, and building layouts that survive every screen size. Mobile Flexbox differs from the web in defaults that will catch you out.

steps.title: Styling and design systems
steps.description: StyleSheet, platform-specific styles, dark mode, safe areas and a reusable component library so the app looks intentional rather than assembled.

steps.title: Navigation
steps.description: Stack, tab and drawer navigators, params, deep linking and typed routes with React Navigation or Expo Router.

steps.title: Lists and virtualisation
steps.description: FlatList and SectionList, keyExtractor, memoised rows and windowing. Long lists are where naive React Native apps visibly stutter.

steps.title: Forms and validation
steps.description: Controlled inputs, keyboard handling, focus management and schema validation. Mobile keyboards create problems the web never has.

steps.title: State management
steps.description: Context for small apps, then Zustand or Redux Toolkit as complexity grows. Pick the smallest tool that handles your real state shape.

steps.title: Data fetching and caching
steps.description: Server state with TanStack Query: caching, background refetching, pagination and optimistic updates, instead of hand-rolled loading flags.

steps.title: Local storage and offline support
steps.description: AsyncStorage, MMKV, SQLite and offline-first sync strategies. Mobile networks fail constantly and your app should not.

steps.title: Authentication flows
steps.description: Token storage in secure keychain storage, refresh flows, biometric unlock and social sign-in. Never keep tokens in AsyncStorage.

steps.title: Native device APIs
steps.description: Camera, geolocation, notifications, file system and sensors, together with the permission flows each platform requires.

steps.title: Push notifications
steps.description: Device tokens, foreground and background handling, deep linking from a notification, and the different behaviour on iOS and Android.

steps.title: Animations and gestures
steps.description: Reanimated and Gesture Handler for animations that run on the UI thread, plus shared element transitions. Smoothness is a feature.

steps.title: Writing native modules
steps.description: Bridge to Swift, Kotlin or Java when no library exists, and understand the new architecture with TurboModules and Fabric.

steps.title: Performance profiling
steps.description: Find dropped frames, excessive re-renders and bridge congestion with Flipper and the React DevTools profiler. Measure before optimising.

steps.title: App size and startup time
steps.description: Hermes, bundle splitting, image optimisation and lazy loading. First launch is the impression users judge you on.

steps.title: Testing
steps.description: Unit tests with Jest, component tests with React Native Testing Library and end-to-end flows with Detox or Maestro.

steps.title: Debugging and crash reporting
steps.description: Source-mapped stack traces, breadcrumbs and release-health monitoring so you can diagnose crashes on devices you will never hold.

steps.title: Accessibility
steps.description: Screen reader labels, focus order, touch target sizes and dynamic type. Also a legal requirement in a growing number of markets.

steps.title: Builds and code signing
steps.description: Provisioning profiles, certificates, keystores and automated cloud builds. Signing is the step that reliably blocks first releases.

steps.title: Continuous delivery and OTA updates
steps.description: Automate builds and distribution to TestFlight and Play Console tracks, and ship JavaScript-only fixes over the air within store rules.

steps.title: Store submission and review
steps.description: Store listings, screenshots, privacy nutrition labels, data safety forms and the review rules that cause most rejections.

steps.title: Analytics and product iteration
steps.description: Event tracking, funnels, crash-free rate and staged rollouts, so the next release is driven by evidence rather than opinion.

steps.title: Capstone: ship a real app to both stores
steps.description: Build an app with authentication, offline support, push notifications and tests, then publish it to the App Store and Play Store and iterate on real feedback.
